source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Citrus canker is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri, and can affect leaves, branches, fruit, and stems. The bacterium can survive for over a year in dead branch material that has fallen to the ground, which then re-infects the orchard. On leaves it produces light-brown spotted lesions with a corky, water-soaked-looking raised texture.

Control measures given in the source:
1) Cut off and burn/destroy affected plant parts.
2) Fungicide spray: copper chloride trihydroxide 85% WP at 45-60 g per 20 L water, or a Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) as an alternative.
